02 / Brand foundations proposed language

Competence without complexity.

An engineering-led brand should inspire confidence without forcing customers to learn engineering to make a decision. The strategic centre is understandable expertise.

Internal organising thought

Make complex energy simple.
Make progress visible.

This line guides design and communication. It is not an approved replacement for the existing corporate signature.

PURPOSEHelp households and organisations benefit from dependable cleaner energy.
PROMISEClear guidance, capable execution and responsible support.
PERSONALITYCompetent · Transparent · Optimistic · Human · Measured

Show the proof

Prefer verified case studies, site photography and process explanations over superlatives.

Speak plainly

Use customer outcomes first; introduce technical specifics where needed.

Leave space

Every layout has a primary idea, one support point and a next action.

COMMERCIAL NORTH STAR / PROPOSEDBe the name customers remember, recommend and contact when energy decisions become real.
  • Visual consistency builds recall.
  • Project proof creates preference.
  • Sales-ready content connects trust to action.
  • Do not replace the existing corporate signature with this internal strategy statement.
Brand strategy supplement / shared cross-platform communication system

One URE identity. Three distinct communication roles.

A practical content system for U R ENERGY: Trust makes people willing to consider URE. Emotion makes them care by recognising a real pain point, without offering a solution. Logic helps them justify the decision. The three pillars strengthen the existing brand guidelines rather than changing them.

Brand strategy ≠ content calendar

The strategy defines URE’s enduring meaning, buyer relevance and recognisable behaviour. Individual posts and campaigns are applications of that strategy. All channels retain the same logo, colour, typography, voice and claim-verification rules already documented in this guideline.

Working proposal · leadership sign-off required

This is a URE-specific working brand strategy. Proposed positioning requires leadership approval; project evidence, claims and service details must be verified before publication.

Our own URE brand foundation: why the work matters, how we approach it and what the business offers. The nested circles are an editable URE design element, with language proposed for internal review.

The editorial roles are deliberate, not interchangeable: Trust earns consideration; Emotion earns attention to the customer’s unresolved problem; Logic supports a well-informed decision. A piece of content may touch multiple pillars, but should lead with one.

Content architecture / TRUST

Evidence before adjectives.

One clearly defined communication task, one credible visual family and one meaningful response.

PILLAR 01 / 03
Job of the post

Make a prospective customer willing to consider URE by showing something verifiable.

Proof it needs

A documented installation, permissioned customer statement, genuine team explanation or approved project details.

Visual family

Documentary: authentic site photos, context captions, material/process details.

Hook pattern

“What goes into a URE installation before the panels are switched on?”

Natural next step

See an approved installation story or request actual project credentials.

Never do

Unverified “No.1” claims, staged success stories, AI images passed off as URE projects.

How to read results

Qualified enquiries referencing a project; meaningful saves; proof-page visits; evidence recall.

Content architecture / EMOTION

Recognise the pain. Do not resolve it.

This is not a disguised sales post. Keep the customer’s lived difficulty at the centre.

PILLAR 02 / 03
Job of the post

Make people care by reflecting a real, unresolved customer pain point. Do not solve it in this post.

Proof it needs

A believable real-life pain point supported by customer insight or an observed situation—not invented testimonials or financial figures.

Visual family

Human editorial: a real Indian homeowner reviewing an electricity bill; a facility manager under budget pressure; a business owner balancing rising costs. No product hero image.

Hook pattern

“The electricity bill arrived. The budget was already stretched.”

Natural next step

End with recognition or a question: “Does this feel familiar?” No solution, quote request, lead form or sales CTA.

Never do

Do not show the solar solution, panels, installation team, price offer, pitch or happy after-scene. No exaggerated suffering or invented bill values.

How to read results

Meaningful comments about the same pain point, saves, shares, watch-through and audience resonance—not immediate leads.

URE / THE HUMAN DECISION — EMOTION
The bill increased. The worries did too.
REAL CUSTOMER-CONTEXT PHOTOGRAPH
Customer reviewing bills or business overheads — no solar imagery
RECOGNITION, NOT FEAR02 / 03

Conceptual layout study, not a finished campaign. Replace the labelled asset with approved evidence before publishing.

Content architecture / LOGIC

Clarity makes the decision easier.

One clearly defined communication task, one credible visual family and one meaningful response.

PILLAR 03 / 03
Job of the post

Give a prospect the information needed to explain and justify an energy decision.

Proof it needs

Verified specifications, documented inclusions, labelled assumptions, current applicable policy/source.

Visual family

Decision editorial: two-column comparison, simple data graphics, disciplined labels.

Hook pattern

“Same solar capacity. Different quotation. What changes the scope?”

Natural next step

After explaining the facts, invite the buyer to compare a project-specific proposal or clarify requirements.

Never do

Invented ROI, universal savings, unlabeled assumptions, oversimplified engineering claims.

How to read results

Qualified questions, guide downloads, technical consultation requests and proposal progression.

URE / DECISION DESK — LOGIC
Same capacity.
Different scope.
VERIFIED SIDE-BY-SIDE COMPARISON
Inclusions, exclusions, assumptions
No fictional prices or performance
COMPARE WITH CLARITY03 / 03

Conceptual layout study, not a finished campaign. Replace the labelled asset with approved evidence before publishing.

Example: industrial energy costs. Trust: document an approved URE project and the work involved. Emotion: show the finance manager facing rising costs and accountability, without introducing any solution. Logic: explain which verified inputs and exclusions influence the commercial comparison. Each is a distinct post with a different audience task.

Compete on proof.
Not on louder promises.

URE should win preference with real project proof, region-specific communication, clear quotations and a fast enquiry experience. SolarSquare is an external positioning reference, not a model to copy or evidence of superior conversion.

08 / Visual grammar

Let the work
speak for itself.

The foundation of URE imagery is real people, real installations and natural light. Use abstract solar-grid geometry for structure, not to disguise weak photography.

Proposed ownable solar-array geometry, generated as vector artwork. It illustrates the layout principle without pretending to depict a real installation.

PHOTOGRAPHYAuthentic Indian homes, workshops, rooftops, factories and engineering teams. Favour believable daylight, real skin tones and useful contextual detail.
COMPOSITIONOne main focal point. Choose crop before placing type; allow an actual 15–20% text-safe region.
GRAPHICSControlled grid geometry, clean numbered markers and simple technical charts. Avoid gratuitous 3D or glass effects.
AI CONTENTNever invent installations, customer endorsements, certificates, warranty claims or site-specific equipment imagery and present them as documentary fact.

Framing quality rules

01 / Crop

Never crop faces, hands, panels or installed equipment arbitrarily. Keep the subject complete where function matters.

02 / Contrast

Use clear text zones or solid surfaces, not harsh gradients behind every caption.

03 / Edit

Correct exposure and white balance consistently. Never over-sharpen, oversaturate or fabricate location-specific details.

09 / Verbal identity

Confident.
Never exaggerated.

A URE communication should sound like a knowledgeable person explaining something important—not an ad full of slogans.

On brand

“Know what goes into your solar quote.”

Specific, useful, clear and conversation-opening.

Off brand

“India’s No. 1 unbeatable solar revolution!”

Unverified superiority, empty intensity and little customer value.

Context Communication rule Example direction
Residential Problem → helpful explanation → next action Understand savings and installation steps
B2B Capability → verified proof → project discussion What a technically complete EPC quote includes
Partners Opportunity → programme details → qualification Grow with a supportive solar partner network
Festive Culture first, natural brand connection second Meaningful connection, not forced solar wordplay

Approved corporate signature in supplied logo: “GENERATE | TRANSMIT | TRANSFORM”. Do not replace it with working copy from this manual.

RESPONSE-FIRST COPY SYSTEMHook → verified reason → customer payoff → one CTA.
  • Do
    “Planning rooftop solar in Surat? Send your city and approximate bill; our team can explain the next step.”
  • Avoid
    “Guaranteed zero bill! Offer ends tonight!” unless every condition is substantiated and approved. Comments must be answered with useful information, not engagement bait. Avoid false scarcity, exaggerated savings and artificial testimonials.

11 / CMO commercial operating model · proposed

Attention is valuable.
Pipeline is the objective.

The promoter and CMO prioritise social-led demand, sales conversations and qualified leads. URE should make conversion possible in every campaign, while giving people a reason to share, save, comment or repost. Commercial outcomes are the objective; not every post needs an aggressive sales headline.

01 / SEEA recognisable roof.

Own a visual moment customers recognise and send to somebody else.

02 / BELIEVEEvidence carries the current.

Show the real installation, people, challenge and outcome—not abstract claims.

03 / ACTOne clear next connection.

A relevant DM, call or consultation, routed to one owner.

04 / GROWTurn interest into a project.

Qualify, follow up, quote and learn from closed and lost opportunities.

60%Direct sales & proof35% direct conversion + 25% proof / objection handling
20%Share-worthy engagementRelevant situations, regional stories and discussion
10%Brand recognitionAchievements, people, presence
10%Decision supportPractical buyer FAQs, not generic lessons

Starting editorial hypothesis. Review after a four-to-six-week content test; never report these percentages as platform performance facts.

01 / STOP THE SCROLL

Share-worthy tension

A real objection, surprising comparison or relatable situation. Measure qualified reach, sends/shares and profile visits.

02 / SHOW THE REASON

Commercial proof

Verified installations, real team, demonstration, transparent process, client-permitted evidence. Measure saves, case-study views and relevant comments.

03 / OPEN THE DOOR

Conversation trigger

One specific CTA: DM your city and monthly bill; request a site discussion; ask for partner criteria. Measure tracked DMs, form submissions and calls.

04 / HANDLE THE LEAD

Fast, accurate follow-up

Capture need, service location, project scale, timeframe, contact permission and owner. Measure contacted and qualified leads, then quotes and wins.

The qualified-lead definition must differ by audience.

Lane Minimum intake Next action Revenue reporting
Residential City / PIN, bill range, roof ownership/type, preferred contact, consent Eligibility & technical consultation Site visits → quotations → installations
C&I Company, location, approximate demand / roof or site, decision role, timeline Technical discovery call Opportunity value → proposals → awarded projects
Channel partner Territory, business model, current experience, capability, contact permission Partner qualification Approved partners → active partner-sourced sales

Weekly CMO dashboard — metric hierarchy

Layer Track Interpretation
Distribution Reach, non-follower reach, shares/sends, reposts Content is circulating beyond followers
Consideration Saves, profile views, link clicks, genuine comments Relevant buyers are moving toward evaluation
Demand Unique DMs, WhatsApp starts, calls, forms Social generated observable enquiries; deduplicate
Quality Qualified leads / total leads, contacted rate, response time Sales usefulness, not just lead volume
Commercial Site visits, proposals, conversion rate, attributed pipeline, won revenue Actual business contribution

Attribution: use channel + campaign + creative + language + format IDs; source-tag tracked links and enquiry records. Obtain permission for contact, avoid exposing personal data, and apply the same deduplication policy across platforms. Never guarantee organic reach or sale outcomes.

14 / Commercial content families

Not more templates.
Better conversion stories.

Every family is a reusable story architecture. The creative brief must specify a single audience, tension, verified proof, desired action, visual source, language and sales owner. The brand stays consistent; the story and content hierarchy change.

Family Opening / concept Evidence and visual Organic CTA and measure

T02 / Objection-led carousel “Two quotations. Same capacity. What’s different?” Line-by-line anonymised comparison; explain scope honestly Save / request consultation → shares, leads

good decisions.

19 / Editorial, brand & production quality audit

Quality isn't a score.
It's a release decision.

This is URE's mandatory pre-publication quality gate. It protects brand recognition, commercial accuracy, regional-language clarity and conversion readiness. The same standard applies to a price-led offer, an Instagram Reel, a Gujarati Story, a LinkedIn EPC case study and printed collateral.

What does this section tell the team?
  • It tells the designer what good looks like , the reviewer what to verify , the CMO what is ready to publish , and the sales team what must happen after a lead responds .
  • A design is not approved merely because it looks premium or scores well aesthetically.

A. Nine release gates

Each item is scored 0–10 with attached evidence. All critical gates require 9.0 or higher; a score below 9 or missing evidence means Revise / Hold. Ratings are assigned by named reviewers, not automatically generated. The editable checkboxes below are for the team’s working review and are not proof of compliance by themselves.

Gate Pass condition Owner / evidence Critical?
01 · Brand identity Approved master logo, clear space, exact brand wording, type and colour hierarchy Brand manager · signed artwork / logo source Yes
02 · Message & strategy One audience, one purpose, credible brand position and correct content stage CMO / content lead · approved brief Yes
03 · Sales action Relevant next action, live lead destination, response owner and qualification route Sales lead · tested link / CRM route Yes
04 · Factual accuracy Claims, prices, taxes, subsidy terms, warranties, dates and project results verified Technical + commercial · evidence register Yes
05 · Creative execution Compelling hook, correct photo/crop, legible hierarchy, native format and intentional CTA Creative director · export inspection Yes
06 · Language & culture English / Gujarati / Telugu reviewed by fluent editor; no text clipping or accidental mixed scripts Language reviewer · signed translation Yes
07 · Accessibility Readable captions, useful alt text, contrast, subtitles and mobile safe zones Design QA · viewport / caption checks Yes
08 · Production & print Correct dimensions, no clipping; HTML mobile reviewed and A4 PDF visually proofed Production lead · screenshots / PDF proof Yes
09 · Learning readiness Post ID, tracking tags, engagement baseline, lead quality measure and review date Marketing ops · tracking sheet No

B. Release checklist

RELEASE LOGIC

Publish only when all critical gates pass.

9.0–10: Ready, subject to sign-off. 8.0–8.9: Revise before release. Below 8: Rework. Missing evidence: Hold regardless of score.

POST-PUBLISH

Measure relevance, not vanity alone.

Review shares, saves and thoughtful comments alongside qualified conversations, consultation bookings, quotes and won revenue. Record insights at 48 hours, 7 days and 30 days.

Status: this manual is a proposed operating standard. Exact corporate brand assets and commercial claims still require URE approval. No claimed 9+/10 production score is valid without real testing and reviewer sign-off.
